hypothesis: The abort-and-send intermittent (queue.rs:545 'the session never went idle after the abort', 1/3 quiet-VM solo, 600.98s wall) is a lost abort in the [runner-pickup, agent-run-registration) window, not a flake: the delivery's cancel flag is consulted nowhere before the run registers, so agent.abort() no-ops on the empty run slot and the turn serves its full provider hold.
approach: Reproduced at rate with a state-dumping harness (worker/turn_stream_tests/abort_idle_race.rs: the same admission sequence, delayMs 3000, a 300ms idle window, dumps on every miss), then fixed at the engine admission seam: the delivery's cancel flag (the worker's abort probe, pickup-cleared, so true at the consult = 'an abort landed after this delivery's pickup') is consulted (1) in run_model_turn after the session build, before the retry/failover driver (-> TurnResult::Aborted -> run_turns' abort arm -> DoneAborted), and (2) at run_turn_once's admission future head (the last stop before the registration) -> Ok(TurnOnce::Aborted) so the retry driver never re-classifies the raced turn. The runner's fallback agent_end now gates on the abort flag too (an aborted settle keeps the compact-interrupt probe's suppressed-run silence). The family test gained TS ENG-5991's positive-signal sync (the run-slot registration, not core.busy+400ms).
parity_notes: TS's registration gap is microscopic (session built at construction, admission synchronous on the event loop); the Rust port's lazy per-worker session build inside the delivery widened it to the whole admission prefix - the consult restores TS-equivalent semantics for a cancel racing the admission. Disclosed corner: the probe combines abort_requested || retry_abort_requested (the engine's existing delivery-cancel semantic at the retry-sleep and boundary consults); an abort_retry landing alone in an admission prefix aborts the delivery where TS's abortRetry-with-no-retry-in-flight no-ops (wire-only corner).
